# Passenger Agent OS — Progress

Append-only worklog. Every agent adds an entry when it finishes a task — what shipped, what it learned, what it left behind. **Newest first — insert your entry at the top, never append at end-of-file** (L-003). `BOARD.md` holds current state; this holds history.

Entry format:

```
### YYYY-MM-DD — <agent> — <task id> <short title>
- **Did:** what actually changed (files, migrations, issue IDs)
- **Evidence:** build/test output, screenshots, review verdicts
- **Left behind:** follow-ups, known gaps, anything the next agent needs
```

- **`waitForToastState` is a genuine positive signal, not a disguised sleep.** Read it against `LocalQACoordinator.swift`: both the coordinator's `start()`/`for await` loop and the test are `@MainActor`-isolated, so `await Task.yield()` in a bounded `while !predicate` loop actually gives the scheduler a real chance to run the coordinator's pending work each turn and returns the instant `toastState` observably changes — not a longer guess at a fixed window. `deadline`/`ContinuousClock` bounds it at 5s and the loop returns cleanly (not throws) on timeout, so a genuine hang fails via the subsequent `#expect` with a real state mismatch, not an uncaught hang. ### 2026-08-08 — ios-developer — T-066/PAS-62 `LocalQACoordinatorTests` flaky sleep-based sync — fixed, verified under real concurrent load

- **Did:** `passenger-code e09bef7` (fast-forwarded onto `main`, rebased cleanly onto `2a2a4ac`/T-081's just-landed merge — no conflicts, my diff touches only `PassengerTests/LocalQACoordinatorTests.swift`). `offerEligibleEventAsks` and `secondEventWhileAskingIsDropped` synchronized the coordinator's async `for await` loop with a hardcoded `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(50))` — a fixed window not always enough under machine load (PAS-62's own diagnosis, confirmed). Replaced with a new `waitForToastState(on:until:timeout:)` helper: repeatedly yields the MainActor executor and re-checks the real `toastState` until the predicate holds, bounded by a 5s safety-net timeout that is not itself the synchronization mechanism (it should essentially never fire). This resolves the instant the coordinator's loop actually processes the event, whatever that takes, rather than gambling on a fixed delay. `secondEventWhileAskingIsDropped`'s second wait (after yielding the dropped event) has no positive completion signal to key off — a drop never mutates `toastState` (TRD §11 C11) — so it's a small bounded `Task.yield()` loop, disclosed in-code as best-effort coverage rather than a correctness requirement, since `AsyncStream`'s FIFO ordering already makes the assertion (`toastState == .asking(first)`) stable regardless of whether the second event has been dequeued yet.
- **Evidence, load-insensitivity — not asserted, measured:** ran the two named tests 20x back-to-back, foreground, against real concurrent load from two other in-flight dispatches (T-068, T-081) sharing this machine — `uptime` load averages sampled 75 to 501 across the run (not simulated; genuinely present). Of 20 attempts, 17 actually executed the two tests; all 17/17 passed, each in 1–6ms. The 3 non-executions were simulator-launch infrastructure errors (`FBSOpenApplicationServiceErrorDomain`/"Busy" ×2, a resource-bundle race ×1) that occurred before any test code ran — not assertion failures, not caused by this diff; a known simulator-contention pathology at this load level, separate from the sleep-based sync bug this task fixes. Whenever the tests actually ran, they were 100% consistent regardless of load level, which is the argument for load-insensitivity: the new signal keys off the real state (`toastState`), not a calibrated delay, so it has no "window" for load to blow through — the only failure mode left is the executor never getting a turn at all, which would starve the whole test process, not just this one.
- **Evidence, full suite:** first full-suite attempt (under load ~500) hit an app **crash** mid-`HeatPaletteTests` with cascading "Crash: Passenger at …" failure-attribution to everything after it in that process launch (`xcresult` showed 424/527 "failed") — the documented "Restarting after unexpected exit, crash, or test timeout" simulator-contention pathology (`passenger-code/CLAUDE.md`'s Simulator facts), not a real regression; discarded as untrustworthy rather than reported. Re-ran clean: **`PassengerTests` 469/469 passed, 0 failures, 0 crashes** (`✔ Test run with 469 tests in 81 suites passed`). `PassengerUITests`: 31/32 passed — the one failure, `SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests.testReadoutNeverIntersectsTheNavRowAtDefaultTextSize()`, is in a file this diff never touches (`git diff HEAD` on it is empty) and reproduced identically (same "+12 hours, HH:00 missing next day qualifier" shape) in both full-suite runs; it sits on the exact HourSlider-in-search-modal surface T-081 just removed on `main` moments before this task's own final verify run, so it's very likely already stale/moot post-T-081 rather than a fresh finding — not chased further, out of this task's scope. `ScenicWalkBundleInvariantTests.falseFlagCountAndTotal` (the pre-flagged T-076/PAS-72 case) did not appear as a failure in either run.
- **Confirmed on the actual merged commit**, not just the pre-rebase one: re-ran `LocalQACoordinatorTests` (6/6 passed) directly against `e09bef7` after the fast-forward.
- **Left behind:** none for this task. Worth a look for whoever owns `T-081`/`PAS-76` follow-up: `SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests` may now be dead-surface and safe to delete/retarget, per the note above — not filed as a new finding since it's plausibly already this task's own known consequence.

### 2026-08-08 — ios-code-reviewer — T-068/PAS-64 code review: APPROVE WITH MINORS

- **Did:** Source-only review (no rebuild/rerun — diff is a single test file, 59 insertions/3 deletions, no production surface touched; `ios-developer`'s own dispatch already produced a clean isolated-worktree 501/502 run with the 1 failure independently triaged as the pre-existing `SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests` wall-clock flake, cross-checked against the 2026-08-07 finding-4 entry — reviewed source-only per the task's own house-convention allowance for small isolated fixes).
- **Verified against ground truth, not the commit message alone:**
  - `git show --stat 01bdcd0` and `git diff --stat 7351bd5 01bdcd0` both confirm the diff touches exactly one file, `PassengerTests/PassportBundleInvariantTests.swift` — no change to the designated-Hood set, `LocalStatus.threshold`, or any production file. Scope discipline holds.
  - Read `prds/hood-dataset/hood-dataset.md` req 5's pass/fail bullet directly (line 55, added at T-047/PAS-34 acceptance): "for each Hood carrying `designated_for_progression: true`, its count of `places-tel-aviv.json` rows with `permanently_closed: false` is ≥ `LocalStatus.threshold`." The diff's new check is `catalog.places(in: hood.id).filter { !$0.permanentlyClosed }.count >= LocalStatus.threshold` — matches the spec's pass condition exactly, not just the commit message's paraphrase of it.
  - Traced `regressionCountsVisitableNotRawPlaces` by hand: fixture builds `threshold - 1` open places + 1 closed place. `rawCount == threshold` (2, given `LocalStatus.threshold == 2`) → old buggy `rawCount >= threshold` reads true, a false pass; `visitableCount == threshold - 1` (1) → new check `visitableCount >= threshold` reads false, correctly short. Matches the commit's stated reasoning exactly.
  - Confirmed compile-plausibility of the new fixture code against the real signatures it depends on: `Place`'s memberwise init (`Passenger/Places/Place.swift`) takes `id/name/category/hoodID/coordinate/permanentlyClosed/placeType` with `isTouristTrap`/`keywords` defaulted — matches the test's call sites; `PlaceCategory.eatDrink` exists (`Passenger/Places/PlaceCategory.swift`); `PlaceCatalog.places(in hoodID: String) -> [Place]` exists (`Passenger/Places/PlaceCatalog.swift:69`) and is unchanged.
  - Requirement-completeness check (L-009 discipline): confirmed this is purely a build-time bundle-invariant test, not a user-facing runtime path. The actual in-app "Local" computation (`Passenger/Passport/PassportComposition.swift:57-58`, `LocalStatus.isLocal(beenCount:)`) is driven by a user's own visit history (`beenCount`), not by scanning `PlaceCatalog` against `permanentlyClosed` — a structurally separate mechanism from the invariant this task fixes. No parallel runtime bug exists that this diff should have touched but didn't.
- **Minor finding (non-blocking):** `regressionCountsVisitableNotRawPlaces` proves the bug at the *value* level (asserts `rawCount`/`visitableCount` directly against a fixture) rather than the *execution* level — it never calls the real `everyDesignatedHoodMeetsThreshold`, `PlaceCatalog`, or `HoodCatalog`. This is honestly disclosed in the test's own doc comment ("it doesn't call `PlaceCatalog`/`HoodCatalog`... this test pins down as a value, not as a code path") and is a reasonable trade-off given `PlaceCatalog` loads from the real bundle rather than an injectable fixture — but it means a future regression that reintroduces raw counting into `everyDesignatedHoodMeetsThreshold` itself would not be caught by this new test; only direct inspection of that function would catch it. Worth a follow-up if `PlaceCatalog` ever grows fixture-injectability, not worth blocking on now.
- **Verdict: APPROVE WITH MINORS.** Fix is correct, scope-disciplined, matches the spec it claims to implement, and the regression test's math is sound by hand-trace.

### 2026-08-07 — ios-code-reviewer — T-084/`PAS-79` review: EventLayer marker-nudge/handleTap fix — APPROVE WITH MINORS (geometry and race mechanism independently confirmed by hand; no live repro obtained by this review either)

- **Did:** Reviewed `passenger-code 7975dc4` against `ios-developer`'s static-analysis-only root cause per the dispatch brief's explicit instruction to probe the central claim rather than accept it. Read `EventLayer.swift`, `MapScreen.swift` (full `handleTap`, `mapPointTolerance`, the `.simultaneousGesture` composition and its FB19394663 doc comment), `EventHitTester.swift`, and the new `EventPlaceHitTestRaceTests.swift` in full.
- **Geometry independently re-derived, not just read:** `markerAnchor = UnitPoint(0.5, 0.5 − 18/44) ≈ (0.5, 0.091)`. Working through what an `Annotation` anchor means (the fraction of the content box that coincides with `coordinate`), the 44×44 box's screen top sits at `coordinate − 0.091×44 ≈ coordinate − 4pt` and its bottom at `coordinate + 40pt` — matching `ios-developer`'s own numbers exactly, derived independently rather than copied. `EventHitTester.event(at:tolerance:)` is a plain circular `MKMapPoint.distance(to:) <= tolerance` check (confirmed by reading it), and `mapPointTolerance` converts a screen-point distance to a map-point distance isotropically off Web Mercator's local conformality (valid — Mercator preserves local aspect ratio, so a horizontal-only calibration applies equally to vertical/diagonal distance). Under the **old** flat 22pt tolerance: box points from `y≈−4` to `y≈22` (on-axis) fall inside a 22pt circle around `coordinate`, but `y≈22` to `y≈40` — roughly the bottom 41% of the visible 44pt box, i.e., genuinely "the marker's own visible lower half" as the commit claims — fall outside it, and diagonal/off-center points inside that lower region fall outside even sooner. This is not "18 vs 22 sounds plausible" hand-waving; a materially-sized region of the drawn, tappable box is provably outside the old tolerance. Under the **fix's** widened tolerance (22+18=40): notably, `40` exactly equals the box's own bottom-edge offset (`nudge + boxHeight/2 = 18+22 = 40`, and `boxHeight/2` happens to equal the original 22pt tolerance) — the widened radius reaches the box's vertical center-line all the way to its bottom edge on-axis, though it still doesn't reach the box's far bottom corners (a circle can't fully cover a rectangle) — an approximation the fix doesn't overclaim, and a real but non-blocking residual gap.
- **Race mechanism independently confirmed, not taken on faith:** the claim that `handleTap`'s `SpatialTapGesture` fires for the *same physical touch* as the marker `Button`, not as an exclusive alternative, is corroborated by two **pre-existing** doc comments this diff did not write: `MapScreen.swift`'s `.simultaneousGesture` modifier (line ~362) — "`.onTapGesture` does not fire on `Map`... `SpatialTapGesture` via `.simultaneousGesture`... MapKit's own pan/pinch handling stays live" — and `handleTap`'s own pre-existing docstring (line ~1050) already documenting that "`MapScreen.swift`'s greedy `SpatialTapGesture` would fire alongside the marker's own `Button`" for the event branch, and relying on `DetailRouter.openEvent` idempotency to make that safe *when both branches agree*. That reliance is exactly the gap PAS-79 exploits: idempotency only helps when both calls resolve to the same destination; when the gesture branch misses and falls through to `openHood`, the two calls disagree and last-call-wins, which SwiftUI does not document an ordering guarantee for. So both halves of the claim — parallel firing, and mutually-exclusive-destination overwrite — are independently traceable to code and comments outside this commit, not just this session's own reasoning.
- **Not independently live-confirmed.** Did not attempt a build/simulator repro this review — same limitation the developer disclosed, not resolved here. Did not find seed data/a default-view path around the `PAS-80` hour-slider seam in the time available; did not pursue further given the strength of the independent geometric/mechanism confirmation above. This is a real gap, disclosed plainly rather than papered over.
- **Other passes:** TRD/scope — fix stays entirely inside the existing T-034 hit-test contract (event > place > hood precedence, TRD §4.5/D7), no deviation. Security/privacy — no location logging/caching changes. Regression risk — widening only the event branch's tolerance could in principle steal a tap meant for a nearby place pin that isn't the event's own venue, but the event count is capped at ≤12 citywide (existing comment, `MapScreen.swift` ~line 327), so the exposure is small and the trade-off (fixing a `DetailRouter`-clobbering bug) is reasonable. Maintainability — the exposed `EventLayer.markerVerticalNudge` constant is reused rather than duplicated, comments at both use sites cross-reference each other, consistent with existing file idioms.
- **Verdict: APPROVE WITH MINORS.** The central claim is not merely "plausible" — the geometry checks out under independent hand computation with matching numbers, and the race mechanism is corroborated by comments predating this fix. Given `qa`/`PAS-79`'s own DoD requirement 2 already lines up with what this mechanism predicts, this clears the bar for shipping, but the lack of any live confirmation (developer's and mine) means it should still get a live check the moment `PAS-80`'s seam is fixed, rather than being treated as fully closed. Minor: the residual circular-vs-rectangular corner gap noted above is not worth blocking on.
- **Left behind:** `BOARD.md` T-084 moved to `qa`. Asked `qa` to attempt a live check of this specific fix (before/after tap behavior on a visible event marker) if any path around `PAS-80`'s hour-slider seam becomes available, and otherwise to carry forward the same "strong hypothesis, not confirmed live" framing into acceptance.

### 2026-08-07 — ios-developer — T-084/`PAS-79` build: EventLayer marker-nudge/handleTap tolerance mismatch fixed (static analysis only, no live repro)

- **Did:** Read `BOARD.md`'s T-084 row and `PAS-79`'s full Linear issue first, per protocol — explicitly briefed to avoid the hour-slider repro seam (`PAS-80`, has defeated 4 prior sessions) and to prefer static/code-level analysis. Traced `EventLayer` → `MapScreen.handleTap`/`DetailRouter.openEvent`, the exact path `qa`'s `PAS-78` recheck confirmed never touches `SearchOverlay`/`chrome`. Found a real, source-provable defect: `EventLayer`'s round-3 redesign (T-062/PAS-58, `EventLayer.swift`'s own extensive comments) draws each marker's whole 44×44 hosting/hit-test box `markerVerticalNudge` (18pt) *below* `event.coordinate`, via `Annotation`'s `anchor:` parameter — deliberately, confirmed by that round's own live measurement, so the visible glyph and the marker's `Button` never separate. But `MapScreen.handleTap`'s parallel `SpatialTapGesture` path (fired for the same physical touch alongside the `Button`'s own tap — `.simultaneousGesture` doesn't consume child gestures, per that file's own doc comment) hit-tested the tapped screen point against the *raw, un-shifted* `event.coordinate`, using the identical flat tolerance (22 screen points) every other branch (place, hood) uses. Since the box mostly extends *downward* from the anchor point (up-extent ≈4pt, down-extent ≈40pt at anchor.y≈0.091), a tap anywhere in the marker's own visible lower half — most of the drawn target — could convert to a map point farther from `event.coordinate` than that flat tolerance allowed, so this second path could genuinely miss the event even on a tap that visibly landed on it. `handleTap`'s `if/else if` chain falls a missed event through to the place branch, then the hood branch — and `HoodHitTester` covers the *entire* city, so a near-miss on event essentially always resolves to `openHood` for that same touch. Both the `Button`'s direct `action` (unconditional, always correctly resolves) and `handleTap`'s `SpatialTapGesture` path fire for one tap; `DetailRouter`'s three destinations are mutually exclusive, so whichever call executes last wins the router's final state — exactly matching a tap that "succeeds" (the `Button`'s `openEvent` genuinely lands) immediately followed by the *other* path silently overwriting it with `openHood`. This is precisely the "reports tappable, wrong/no result" shape `PAS-79`'s own title flagged as `PAS-78`-class, on the confirmed-different code path.
- **Fix (`passenger-code 7975dc4`):** `EventLayer.markerVerticalNudge` changed from `private` to internal `static` (needed at `MapScreen`'s call site, same value, no duplicated constant). `MapScreen.handleTap` now computes `eventTolerance = tolerance + markerNudgeTolerance` (the nudge's own screen-point distance, converted via the same `mapPointTolerance` helper the base tolerance already uses) and passes that widened value to `EventHitTester`, restoring the full intended margin so the `SpatialTapGesture` path agrees with what's actually drawn on screen. Place/hood branches untouched (`PlaceLayer` uses a plain default-anchored `Annotation`, confirmed by reading it — no equivalent offset, no equivalent bug).
- **Not a confirmed live repro.** Per the dispatch's explicit instruction, did not attempt the hour-slider path at all — root cause and fix are derived entirely from static/source analysis (`EventLayer.swift`, `MapScreen.swift`, `EventHitTester.swift`, `PlaceLayer.swift`, `DetailRouter.swift` all read in full). Flagging this plainly rather than overclaiming a confirmed fix, per the dispatch brief's own framing of valid honest outcomes.
- **Test added:** `PassengerTests/EventPlaceHitTestRaceTests.swift` — a narrower-scope unit test against the pure `EventHitTester` geometry `handleTap` actually calls (no UI, no `MapProxy`, no simulator gesture — so it's immune to the slider-driving flakiness `PAS-80` tracks). Demonstrates the tolerance-widening mechanism the fix relies on: every distance in the test is computed live from real `MKMapPoint.distance(to:)` calls (not hand-picked numbers), so the assertions can't silently drift out of sync with the real projection math. Could not unit-test `MapScreen.handleTap` itself (private, requires a live `MapProxy` for screen→map conversion) or reproduce the exact 18pt/22pt production numbers without one — disclosed as a real limitation, not hidden.

### 2026-08-07 — ios-developer — T-083/`PAS-78` build: SearchOverlay result-row tap fixed

- **Did:** Fixed the confirmed silent bug (`qa`'s `passenger-code 84b51da` regression test, `SearchResultRowTapInvestigationTests.swift`): tapping a search-result row dismissed `SearchOverlay` instead of opening the result's detail surface. Per the dispatch brief's warning, the shared tree had `main` checked out with a concurrent session's uncommitted `T-077`/`PAS-51` WIP live in `SearchOverlay.swift` (also `Hood.swift`, `HoodCatalog.swift`, `SearchIndex.swift`, `SearchQuery.swift`, three `PassengerTests` files, `SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests.swift`) — did all work in an isolated worktree (`.claude/worktrees/pas78-fix`, branched from `main` at `84b51da`), never touched the shared tree's files directly during the fix.
  **Investigated qa's own root-cause hypothesis first and it did not reproduce**: dumped the live accessibility tree mid-test (`xcrun xcresulttool export attachments`) during both failing cases. `MapNavRow` was at y≈455-507 (pushed well clear by keyboard avoidance) while the tapped row sat at y≈826-870 — nowhere near overlapping. The qa doc comment's `navRowBandHeight`/`gapAboveNavRow`-band theory, while plausible from a code read, wasn't what was actually happening live.
  **Real root cause, found from the same dump: the row rendered underneath the system keyboard's own window.** The keyboard (always up in the repro, since both tests type a query before tapping) spans the full width down to the true screen bottom; `SearchOverlay`'s `.ignoresSafeArea(edges: .bottom)` used the default `SafeAreaRegions.all`, which ignores the keyboard's safe area along with the container's, so the card never shrunk/repositioned for the keyboard and `resultsArea`'s rows kept rendering flush with the true bottom, straight under the keyboard's topmost window — which silently swallows the touch. `isHittable` still reported `true` since XCUITest only reasons about the app's own hierarchy. Fixed by scoping the call to `.ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .bottom)` — same bottom-flush behavior with no keyboard, now respects the keyboard's inset when one is up.
  That alone wasn't sufficient: fixing case 1 exposed a second, real, separate gap — `handleSearchResultSelection` never called `chrome.dismiss()`, so `SearchOverlay` stayed mounted (covered by, but still present/hit-testable underneath) the newly-opened `PlaceDetailModal`/`HoodSheet`, which is what the tests' `overlayStillPresent` assertion was actually catching. Adding `chrome.dismiss()` directly (not through `dismissSearch()`, which also calls `router.closeHood()` and would immediately close the Hood sheet the same call just opened) surfaced a **third** interaction: `MapScreen`'s existing `.onChange(of: chrome.presented)` → `handlePresentedSurfaceChange` unconditionally called `router.closeHood()` when leaving `.search`, wiping out the just-opened destination before the test could see it. Fixed by narrowing that branch to `newValue != nil` (leaving `.search` for another surface still sweeps a stranded destination, matching existing `MapScreenSearchWiringTests` coverage; a full dismiss-to-`nil` skips the clear only when `router` already holds a fresh selection, which per `openSearch`'s own invariant — it always clears `router` before presenting — is the only way that combination can occur).
  Also widened `SearchAccessibilityTests`' 44pt touch-target check by a `0.01pt` epsilon: the keyboard-safe-area fix adds one more nested keyboard-aware layout pass, and the accumulated `CGFloat` rounding landed a result row's live-measured height at `43.99999999999994` (~6e-14pt under 44) — a strict `>=` comparison flagged it as a false failure; confirmed this test passes on baseline `main` in isolation, so the tolerance widening is scoped to a real, newly-introduced rounding artifact, not a pre-existing gap being papered over.
  Merged the worktree commit to `main` via `git fetch . claude/pas78-fix:main --update-head-ok` rather than a normal `git merge` in the shared tree — `main` was checked out there with the other session's uncommitted `SearchOverlay.swift` edits live, and a normal merge risked a working-tree conflict/clobber on that exact file. This updates only the `main` ref; the shared tree's on-disk files are untouched by the fetch itself. Two of my files (`MapScreen.swift`, `SearchAccessibilityTests.swift`) then showed as locally "modified" purely because the shared tree's checkout was stale relative to the ref move (not real WIP — they were never part of the other session's edit set) — synced those two to the new `HEAD` content directly (confirmed via `diff` they now match `HEAD` byte-for-byte) so the shared tree doesn't carry a confusing false-staged state for the next session. `SearchOverlay.swift` and the other session's 8 WIP files were **not** touched by this sync — confirmed via `git diff --stat` before and after this whole operation that their diffs are byte-identical.
- **Evidence:** Both `SearchResultRowTapInvestigationTests` cases (place row, Hood row) pass in isolation and inside a full-suite run. Preflight: no active `HALT`, `df -h /` 21-31Gi avail throughout (dipped as low as 21Gi mid-run, never near the 5GB floor), `uptime` load spiked to 108-124 during one run (four concurrent sessions building) but the full suite still completed and was re-verified clean on a calmer re-run. - **Did:** Investigated an unconfirmed `designer` finding from the Unowned findings inbox: while driving the app via raw `simctl` coordinate taps for unrelated `PAS-77` verification, `designer` saw tapping a `SearchOverlay` search-result row repeatedly dismiss the overlay instead of selecting the result — flagged as possibly a `simctl`-driving artifact rather than a real bug. Reproduced properly with a real XCUITest `.tap()` on the located element (`app.buttons["<label>"].tap()`), not raw coordinates, per the dispatch brief. Wrote `passenger-code/PassengerUITests/SearchResultRowTapInvestigationTests.swift` (two cases: a place row → expects `PlaceDetailModal`, a Hood row → expects `HoodSheet`), ran it on a dedicated simulator (`qa-searchoverlay-taptest`, iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5), isolated `-derivedDataPath`. This confirms the finding is a real bug, not a `simctl` artifact. Added a frame-diagnostic run (temporary, removed after use) that measured the tapped row's frame at ~(16, 826, 370, 44) in an 874pt-tall window — the row renders essentially flush with the true screen bottom. Traced this against `MapScreen.swift`: `MapNavRow` (z7, ~line 538) is drawn last and documented as "always hit-testable ... renders above all of them" (~line 539-541), reserving a fixed 84pt bottom band (`navRowBandHeight` = 32pt padding + 52pt button); `SearchOverlay.swift`'s own `compactFraction` only adds the matching `navRowBandHeight`/`gapAboveNavRow` reservation for the `.hour` segment, not `.search` — that segment's doc comment (~line 88) assumed a scrolling result list would never need it, which breaks once the visible list is short enough that a row lands inside the unreserved band. Filed **`PAS-78`** in Linear (`Bug` label, `Backlog`, unclaimed — no `owner:*` label, per the dispatch brief: filing is fine directly for a bug discovery, `chief-of-staff` claims/dispatches later) with the full repro steps and root-cause hypothesis. Kept the new test file as regression coverage (trimmed the diagnostic prints, left the frame measurement and hypothesis in its doc comment) rather than deleting it, since the finding is a confirmed real bug. Updated `BOARD.md`'s Unowned findings inbox entry (struck, marked confirmed + filed).
- **Evidence:** `xcodebuild test -project Passenger.xcodeproj -scheme Passenger -destination "id=F40E1C3B-A3AD-492C-B464-1089F915B90C" -only-testing:PassengerUITests/SearchResultRowTapInvestigationTests` — `Executed 2 tests, with 2 failures (0 unexpected)`, both `BUG REPRODUCED` assertion messages. `isHittable == true` on both rows before the tap (ruling out an accessibility-tree miss). ### 2026-08-07 — architect — T-082/`PAS-77` mechanism call: neither tabled candidate — a non-greedy clamp, and the `ViewThatFits` sketch would not have worked

- **Did:** Made the SwiftUI layout-mechanism call `product` explicitly left open (its own worklog entry below, and `modal-shape-standard.md`'s Round-4 section). **Decision: replace `.frame(maxHeight: 480)` with `.frame(maxHeight: 480).fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` on the existing `ScrollView`, identically in all 3 files** — `EventDetailModal.swift:92`, `PlaceDetailModal.swift:104`, `HoodSheet.swift:102`. No `GeometryReader`, no `PreferenceKey`, no `@State`, no `ViewThatFits`. Wrote the decision, the rejection evidence, and a file-by-file build scope into `design/phase-1/modal-shape-standard.md` as a new "Round-4 mechanism decision" sub-section; updated `BOARD.md`'s T-082 row (state → `build (mechanism decided)`, owner → `ios-developer`). **No Swift files touched** — the build is `ios-developer`'s. No TRD written: scoped mechanism call on a non-PRD-gated ticket, per dispatch.
- **Evidence — measured, not reasoned.** Built a SwiftUI layout harness (`NSHostingController.sizeThatFits`, proposal 393×850 — the bottom-aligned `ZStack` case) and swept content heights of 150/300/600/900pt across five constructions. Results: today's `ScrollView{c}.frame(maxHeight: 480)` → **480/480/480/480**. The Round-4 `ViewThatFits` sketch → **480/480/480/480**, identical to today. `ViewThatFits` with the clamp moved inside the fallback branch → 150/300/**600**/480. The chosen clamp → **150/300/480/480**. Also dumped the laid-out view hierarchy at 900pt content: the clamped `ScrollView` is `HostingScrollView` h=480 with a real 480pt `NSClipView` — structurally identical to today's — so `.fixedSize` does not collapse it into a static clipped block.
- **Two findings that change what round 3 believed.** (1) **`.frame(maxHeight:)` is itself greedy** — a bare 150pt block under it measures 480pt. Round 3 attributed the dead band to `ScrollView` alone; the frame is an equal cause, and that is why the `ViewThatFits` sketch fails — the outer clamp re-inflates whatever `ViewThatFits` returns, so the branch choice is irrelevant. Had `ios-developer` built the sketch verbatim off the Round-4 section, the dead band would have been unchanged and only a render would have caught it. (2) **`ViewThatFits` runs its fit test against the proposed height (~850pt), not against 480** — so even with the clamp moved inside the fallback, content between 481 and 850pt renders un-scrolled at full height. That is `PAS-73` (card eats the map) reintroduced through the `PAS-77` fix. No shipped Hood hits it today, but nothing in the mechanism prevents it and `T-075`'s fuller dataset is exactly what would. `GeometryReader`+`PreferenceKey` was rejected as unnecessary rather than unworkable — its costs are real and there is no reason to pay them for what one stateless modifier produces.
- **Why the clamp works:** both `ScrollView` and `.frame(maxHeight:)` are greedy *under a concrete proposal*. `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` removes the concrete vertical proposal, so the frame clamps an *ideal* height instead of inflating a proposed one; `horizontal: false` leaves the width proposal intact, so text wrapping and full-width layout are untouched. Gesture/transition interaction is better than today, not worse: `.offset(y:)` and `.move(edge: .bottom)` translate the card rather than re-proposing its size, so nothing re-triggers measurement — and there is no measurement to re-trigger. On short content the card is shorter than the scroll threshold, so the `ScrollView` has nothing to scroll and the outer `DragGesture` gets the touch cleanly, which incidentally addresses the drag-vs-scroll spot-check `ios-code-reviewer` left for `qa` at round 3, on the 41-of-44 path.
- **Scope answer the dispatch asked for: `HoodSheet` needs no different treatment.** Its "existing fix" is the same greedy `.frame(maxHeight: 480)` as the other two — a cap with no shrink. Three identical one-line edits, one commit. Read all three `card` bodies directly before deciding, plus `RouteControls.swift`: **no `@State` and no `.task`/`onAppear` anywhere inside the card content** (`PlaceDetailModal`'s `.task(id:)` is on `body`, outside `card`), which is what made branch duplication safe to consider in the first place — and moot once `ViewThatFits` was rejected.
- **Disclosed limit of verification — read this before trusting the call.** The harness is macOS AppKit hosting: it measures *sizing*, using the same SwiftUI layout engine, and it does **not** measure gesture behavior. That the clamped `ScrollView` still **scrolls** on iOS at long content is the one claim not proven here. It is written into the standard as a required build-time check with a stated pass condition — card caps at 480pt **and** the last row/button is reachable by scrolling, not merely clipped. **A build that shrinks correctly but clips is a worse regression than the defect being fixed, and no existing test covers it.** Second required check, per `product`'s round-4 note: shrink measured on the *sparsest* case each surface can produce (empty Hood with no blurb, place with permission declined, shortest `EventDetailRows` set) — a typical case passing is not evidence.
- **Left behind:** (1) `ios-developer` builds the 3 one-line edits per the standard's build-scope section; `qa` then measures against criterion 5's procedure plus the scroll check above. (2) `Spacer(minLength: 0)` (`EventDetailModal.swift:82`, `PlaceDetailModal.swift:93`) measured **inert** under this mechanism (190pt with and without, at 150pt content) — removal is optional cleanup, explicitly not part of the fix, though it is the one thing that would silently re-inflate these cards if anyone later drops the `.fixedSize`. (3) `designer`'s parallel Round-4 report is still not reflected anywhere I could find — same gap `product` flagged; `chief` reconciles. (4) Not swept this pass and not mine to claim: **T-071** (backfill-audit of every pre-L-032 TRD §9 table) is still `backlog`; this ticket produced no TRD, so no §9 re-audit was triggered.
- **Git:** `passenger-brain` — `design/phase-1/modal-shape-standard.md`, `agent-os/BOARD.md`, `agent-os/PROGRESS.md`, explicit paths. Not pushed — Aviran-gated (`CLAUDE.md` rule 9). Harness sources are scratchpad-only, not committed.

### 2026-08-07 — product — T-082/`PAS-77` judgment call: fixed 480pt modal cap is **not** an accepted trade-off — needs a content-measured cap across all 3 files

Updated `BOARD.md`'s T-082 row. **No Swift files touched** — mechanism choice is `architect`'s and the fix is `ios-developer`'s; `EventDetailModal.swift`/`PlaceDetailModal.swift` also carry another session's uncommitted WIP in the shared tree, which I left alone (L-035).
- **Evidence — the shipped dataset is what settles this, not taste.** Counted directly from `passenger-code/Passenger/Resources/places-tel-aviv.json` and `hoods-tel-aviv.json`: **9 curated places across 44 hoods**, per-hood distribution `{0 places: 41 hoods, 3 places: 3 hoods}` (only `florentin`, `kerem-hateimanim`, `neve-tzedek` are populated). So **41 of 44 Hoods render `HoodSheet`'s `emptyState`** — icon + one line + "Explore another Hood" button, ~150pt with its `.padding(.vertical, 24)` — inside a 480pt box, and **21 of those 41 have no `blurb` either**, leaving the card body as header + flag line + empty state. The 3 populated Hoods carry 3 rows each (~44pt apiece). **No Hood in shipped V1 fills 480pt.** A defect that fires on 44/44 real data rows is the shipped behavior, not a trade-off. Second point: `PlaceDetailModal`'s worst measured band (60.2%, `ios-developer`'s round-3 pixel scan) was taken with location permission declined — and Passenger has no onboarding by strategy, so "permission not yet granted" is every user's state on first open. The worst number sits on the most-travelled path. Third: accepting it would relax criterion 5 silently while leaving "~25%" on the page — the same class of gap ("a bound the platform used to enforce became nobody's") that criterion 5 was written at round-2 acceptance to close.
- **`HoodSheet` — the extra check the dispatch asked for: it shares the defect, and is the worst of the three by frequency.** Its `card` is the same construction byte-for-byte (`ScrollView { … }.frame(maxHeight: 480)`, `HoodSheet.swift` lines 85–102), the greedy-`ScrollView` mechanism is already empirically proven on that exact shape by round 3's scan of the other two files, and the distribution above shows its content is short for every Hood that exists. **Disclosed limitation:** this is a source-plus-data determination, **not a render** — I did not build or pixel-measure `HoodSheet`. A screenshot could not have changed a verdict the data already settles, and the % is `qa`'s to measure against the new procedure. Do not cite a `HoodSheet` dead-band number from this entry; there isn't one.
- **Deliberately not decided — mechanism.** `PAS-77` requirement 1 names `GeometryReader` + `PreferenceKey`; that works but writes a layout result into `@State` during layout (the usual source of "Modifying state during view update" and size oscillation) and must be built so the outer `DragGesture` and `.transition(.move(edge: .bottom))` don't re-trigger measurement per frame. A stateless alternative worth weighing first: `ViewThatFits(in: .vertical) { content; ScrollView { content } }.frame(maxHeight: 480)` — degrades to exactly today's behavior above 480pt, shrinks to fit below it. **`architect` picks; `product` is not making a SwiftUI layout-mechanism call**, and neither candidate should be implemented on the strength of this entry.
- **Left behind:** (1) Needs `architect` → mechanism, then `ios-developer` → apply to all 3 files, then `qa` → measure per the new procedure on the *sparsest* case each surface can produce (empty Hood with no blurb; place with permission declined; shortest `EventDetailRows` set) — a "typical" case passing is not evidence. (2) `designer`'s parallel report on the same question is not reflected here; `chief` reconciles. (3) The 9-places-across-44-hoods count is itself a content-coverage gap and is the same scarcity `T-075`/`PAS-71` already has open with Aviran — no new row filed, but flagging that the modal-shape symptom and the curation-coverage question share a root cause, and that a fuller dataset would shrink this defect without removing it (`HoodSheet` stays short for any Hood under ~7 places). (4) Out of scope and left settled per `PAS-73`: the 480pt ceiling itself and the dropped `.medium` detent.

Read `BOARD.md`'s T-079 row in full, this file's recent worklog (`ios-developer`'s re-fix entry, `ios-code-reviewer`'s re-review, `qa`'s re-verification), `design/phase-1/modal-shape-standard.md` including my own Correction/criteria sections, and the whole `PAS-73` Linear thread — including the ticket description itself, which mattered (see the detent judgment below). **Inherited nothing** — re-rendered and re-measured every claim myself.
- **Preflight (L-040), re-checked immediately before the build, not at dispatch:** no active `HALT` (`BOARD.md`'s 2026-08-04 line is struck and no new one exists). `df -h /` → 36Gi avail/25% used. `uptime` → load average 48 rising to 122 during the run — high, from other sessions' concurrent `xcodebuild`; handled by taking my own unshared UDID and my own `-derivedDataPath` rather than deferring, and the finding below is a static geometry measurement on a settled frame, not a timing observation, so load can't produce it. Isolated `git worktree` pinned to `08a09fb` (`git status --short` empty before I touched anything) specifically to exclude the live uncommitted `T-077`/`PAS-51` Hood-aliases WIP in the shared tree — never touched it, confirmed identical after. Dedicated simulator `t079-prod-accept` (iPhone 17/iOS 26.5), erased before first install. Simulator-control MCP absent in this unattended run (expected, not retried, per `passenger-code/CLAUDE.md`) — drove the app with a throwaway XCUITest (`ZZProductT079AcceptScratchTests`, 7 surfaces, 7/7 passed, `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`), pulled real PNGs via `xcresulttool export attachments`, measured with my own Python/PIL script and **also looked at the screenshots directly**, which is what caught this round's finding.
- **My round-1 F1 (Group B stopped 34pt short of the bottom) — genuinely fixed.** All 7 surfaces render surface colour on the screen's **last** pixel row (y=2621 of 2622) at x=0, x=mid and x=w−1, `(255,255,255)` on every one, with zero edge-colour transitions in the 250px band above the bottom. Flush and full-width, on Group A and Group B alike. Real fix, not a re-measurement artifact.
- **My round-1 F2 (Group A was never correct on iOS 26) — genuinely fixed.** This was the finding only I caught last round, so I rendered all three Group-A surfaces again rather than assume the fix generalized. `EventDetailModal`, `PlaceDetailModal` and `HoodSheet` no longer render as inset floating cards rounded on all four corners: bottom corners are square and flush to the screen edge, top corners rounded, no map visible left/right/bottom of the card. The iOS 26 Liquid-Glass sheet shape is gone from all three.
- **Blocking finding, new this round: `EventDetailModal` and `PlaceDetailModal` now cover essentially the whole screen.** Card top measured at **y=240px of 2622 = 9% of screen height** (80pt down an 874pt screen) on both. Visually confirmed, not only measured: `PlaceDetailModal` for "Nachum Gutman Museum" renders a title, **one** content row ("Things to do"), then roughly 1,400pt of blank white, then the Directions button pinned at the bottom. `EventDetailModal` for "Rooftop set, Levinsky" is the same with four rows. The map — the app's primary surface — is completely hidden behind a mostly-empty white panel.
  - **Root cause, confirmed in source, not inferred:** both files' `card` is a `VStack` containing `Spacer(minLength: 0)` above the route button, inside a `ZStack(alignment: .bottom)` that fills the screen, with **no `.frame(maxHeight:)` and no `ScrollView`**. Under `.sheet()` + `.presentationDetents` the detent bounded the height and the `Spacer` was harmless; dropping `.sheet()` removed the bound and the `Spacer` became the thing that expands the card to full screen. These are **the only 2 of the 7 modal files with no height cap** — `HoodSheet` received a `ScrollView` + `.frame(maxHeight: 480)` **in this very commit**, `PlacesListOverlay`/`PassportSurface` already had the same 480pt cap, `SearchOverlay` uses a fixed screen fraction.
  - **Measured card tops, same session, same script:** `PlacesListOverlay` and `PassportSurface` 37%, `HoodSheet` 45%, `SearchOverlay` (both segments) 62% — all sane bottom sheets with the map visible above — against **9%** for the two uncapped files. So "one shape app-wide" is satisfied on corner treatment and edge anchoring and is plainly false on proportion.
  - **Why the two prior gates passed it, stated plainly and not as a swipe:** `ios-code-reviewer` *found* this asymmetry and named it precisely, including quoting `HoodSheet`'s own comment saying the identical reasoning applies — then classified it latent after testing whether long content gets **clipped** at AX5. It doesn't. But clipping was never the failure mode; unbounded growth is, and it is live right now against the shipped seed fixtures. `qa` carried the minor forward without re-testing it, resting on that AX5 result. Neither measured card height or viewed the surface's overall proportions. Both did genuinely independent, well-isolated work on everything they did measure.
- **Spec defect fixed in the same commit as the verdict (L-009).** The four pass/fail criteria I myself wrote into `modal-shape-standard.md` at the round-1 REJECT all measure the card's **edges** — full width, flush bottom, top-corners-only, same answer across groups — and none measures its **height**. All four honestly PASS on this build while the surface is visibly wrong, so the gates after me again had nothing objective to fail. Added **criterion 5 — bounded height, the map stays visible above every modal** (card top at or below 40% of screen height; no content-free band taller than ~25% of the card; measure on the left-edge pixel column, since the centre column is interrupted by the nav row), with the measured per-surface results, plus a note that any change removing a platform-supplied constraint owes an explicit replacement for it. Also added a scoped **round-3 fix item 5** naming exactly what to do and why the `Spacer` must stay.
- **The `.medium` detent trade — my own read, asked for explicitly, and it differs from both prior gates in one respect.** I **agree** dropping `.sheet()`/detents does not need to go back to Aviran as a scope question, and I agree for a firmer reason than either gate gave: `PAS-73`'s description is Aviran's own and says shape-consistency; `PAS-48` — the only source of `.medium` — was one of four agent-filed polish tickets whose founder provenance this very file records as *secondhand, no verbatim quote captured, not treated as proof on its own* (2026-08-04 entries; L-013 discipline applied). A verbatim founder ask outranks an unquoted one, so the trade is legitimately an implementation call. **Where I disagree:** both gates called the cost "bounded — a glanceable-map nicety" **without measuring it**, and it is not bounded. `.medium` was the only thing constraining these two cards' height, and removing it without substituting a cap is exactly what produced the blocking finding above. One nuance neither gate raised: `PAS-73`'s description explicitly says *"this ticket is about shape/anchoring, not detent levels"* — which is a reason to be careful with detents, not a licence to delete them, and makes "`.medium` was never named in `PAS-73`" a weaker argument than it looked. So: not a scope escalation, and not something Aviran needs to rule on — an **accepted trade whose cost was never paid**. It becomes payable with a `maxHeight` cap on two files.
- **`PAS-75`:** confirmed fixed and correct, no objection — nav-row button reads "Search and hours," the collision is gone.
- **Not re-run this round, deliberately:** the full suite. Two independent isolated-worktree runs at this commit already agree exactly (494 tests, 1 pre-existing `ScenicWalkBundleInvariantTests` failure tracked at T-076/`PAS-72`), and no test in the suite asserts card height anyway — the gap that mattered here is again one nothing could have failed on, which is what criterion 5 now closes.
- **Verdict: REJECT.** Recommended routing: back to **`build`** / `ios-developer`, scope = round-3 item 5 only (cap `EventDetailModal` and `PlaceDetailModal` at 480pt with a `ScrollView`, matching `HoodSheet`'s treatment in this same commit), then re-verify criterion 5. **Board state and owner not changed by me, and no Linear comment posted** — `chief-of-staff` is the single writer for both; the T-078 row earlier in this arc records me being corrected for exactly that, so the verdict is recorded and the routing recommended, not applied.
- **T-078/`PAS-60` stays held.** My round-1 routing note stands unchanged: it shares this screen, and this screen is not coherent yet. Both should go to `aviran-review` together once the cap lands — not now.
- **Left behind:** worktree, simulator (`t079-prod-accept`) and derived-data all deleted, confirmed via `git worktree list` and `xcrun simctl`; scratch test file deleted before this commit, never staged; `passenger-code`'s shared working tree confirmed byte-identical to how I found it (same 9 files of the other session's Hood-aliases WIP, untouched). Did not remove the 3 other pre-existing registered worktrees — not mine (L-035). No `passenger-code` changes.
- **Git:** `passenger-brain` — `agent-os/BOARD.md` (T-079 row), `agent-os/PROGRESS.md` (this entry), `design/phase-1/modal-shape-standard.md` (criterion 5 + round-3 fix item), explicit paths. Not pushed — Aviran-gated.

### 2026-08-07 — product — T-077/`PAS-51` acceptance: **REJECT** — row 5b's AX3 capture and the F2 wrap check never executed; the known 31pt failure aborts the method before them, and two gates read that silence as a pass

- **Did:** Acceptance pass on `passenger-code 1021428` against `prds/time-slider/TRD.md` v6 §9 row 5b/6(c) and the PRD's own F1/F2 requirement (`time-slider.md` req 5's rendered-legibility bullet, line 55 — "renders unoccluded and unwrapped … at the default text size **and** at the largest supported Dynamic Type size"). Re-derived from source, not from `qa`'s report: read the C16 production diff and the full `SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests.swift` at the tested commit from a clean `git archive` extract (the shared tree carries another session's WIP, **including `HourSlider.swift`**), then ran the suite myself.
- **Preflight (L-040):** re-read `BOARD.md` for a build/test `HALT` before the run — the only one is the 2026-08-04 disk halt, struck/lifted. `df -h /` 38Gi avail, `uptime` 1-min load 2.81. Own simulator (`t077-accept`, created for this pass — the only pre-existing sim, `t078t079-qa`, is another session's), own `-derivedDataPath`, own worktree pinned to `1021428`. Both deleted before finishing, verified gone; other sessions' four worktrees and their simulator left untouched (L-035).
- **Verdict: REJECT.** One cause, two blocking consequences. `assertHourSegmentCapture` runs sub-check **(iii)** (`hourSlider.frame.height >= 44`) *before* the positive control, and the whole helper runs for the `default` capture before the `AX3` capture is ever taken. The class sets `continueAfterFailure = false`. `hourSlider` renders 31pt — known, disclosed, owned by T-081/`PAS-76`. So the method aborts at the **default** capture and never reaches:
  1. **Row 5b capture (b) — the AX3 half — is unrun, not passed.** Its occlusion (i), containment (ii) and ≥44pt (iii) sub-checks never execute. Row 5b requires (a) and (b) "**independently**", and (ii) is what TRD v6 §10 itself calls "the substantive new coverage v6 buys" — the merge-introduced failure mode where `hourContent`'s unclipped top-aligned `VStack` pushes `hourSlider` past the card's bottom edge at AX3. Nothing else in the suite covers it: `testHourSegmentDynamicTypeCeilingBindsAtAX5` does take an AX3 capture, but asserts only existence and non-zero frames, never occlusion or containment.
  2. **The F2 wrap check is unrun** — literally the named second half of this ticket. It is the last statement in the method and covers nothing anywhere else.
- **Evidence (my own run, not inherited):** `xcodebuild test -only-testing:PassengerUITests/SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests` → `Executed 6 tests, with 1 failure`, reproducing `qa`'s 5/6 exactly. The decisive detail neither prior gate reported: inside `testHourSegmentContentStaysUnoccludedAndContainedAcrossTextSizes` the log shows **exactly one** `Launch com.avirangrisaro.passenger`, the failure at `SearchHourSegmentInteractionTests.swift:309` labelled **`[default]`** (`"31.0" is less than "44.0"`), and `Tear Down` at `t = 16.58s`. Two captures cannot happen in one launch: the two-capture `testHourSegmentDynamicTypeCeilingBindsAtAX5` takes 30.97s against this method's 16.63s, and the single-capture `testReadoutNeverIntersectsTheNavRowAtDefaultTextSize` takes 13.31s. The AX3 launch never happened.
- **Not the developer's defect, and not a rebuild of the 31pt gap.** The C16 production diff is correct and the suite is well-constructed — the `mapNavRow` modifier-order fix and the `driveSliderToMaximum` retry are both real finds. The **31pt `HourSlider` gap is disclosed, three-times-confirmed, out of C16's touch-set and separately tracked at T-081/`PAS-76` — this rejection does not ask anyone to fix it.** What it asks for is that the gap stop silently suppressing four sibling sub-checks.
- **Fix, numbered, small:** (1) move sub-check (iii)'s `>= 44` assertion out of `assertHourSegmentCapture` into its own test method covering both captures — it stays visibly red and tracked at T-081, while (i)/(ii)/wrap/positive-control run to completion at **both** text sizes; (2) re-run and report per-sub-check *execution*, not just failure count. **`XCTExpectFailure` is the wrong tool here** — it would turn the method green and bury the 31pt gap.
- **Alternative resolution worth `chief`'s judgment, not mine to take:** T-081 removes `HourSlider` entirely, which makes (iii) moot *and* unblocks the AX3 path — but T-081 is **held until T-077 closes**, and T-077 cannot now close without touching this. That is a circular hold. Un-holding T-081 first may be the cheaper order; flagging it rather than deciding it.
- **Spec gap closed in this same commit (L-009):** the earlier gates did have row 5b's "unrun, not passed" language — they misapplied it. What no gate had is a rule that *assertion ordering under `continueAfterFailure = false` converts "unrun" into "reported as passed."* Added as a fourth standing rule to TRD §9, labelled as added at acceptance and **owed ratification by `architect`**, whose table it is (rule 8 — I did not touch anything Aviran-gated, but the TRD is not mine to rewrite unannounced).
- **PRD `Status:` not flipped** — `time-slider.md` stays at Draft v9 / acceptance REJECT, which remains accurate. No requirement text changed; the requirement was already testable and is simply unverified.
- **Left behind:** T-077 → back to `build` (`ios-developer`), test-file change only, no production code. `chief-of-staff` owns the `PAS-51` verdict and the `BOARD.md` row — not written by me (L-038). The 31pt gap stays parked at T-081; `ScenicWalkBundleInvariantTests` stays parked at T-076.

But `.dynamicTypeSize` is the **app's own environment value**: a launch-argument-gated override at `MapScreen`'s root renders the real card in the real `ZStack` at a real accessibility size, with frames XCUITest can read. That is a rendered check, not a proxy, and it is cheap. **Second, larger defect found while ruling:** v4's row 5b demanded a capture at **AX5**, which became unsatisfiable the moment `HeatModalCard` gained `.dynamicTypeSize(...maxDynamicTypeSize)` at `.accessibility3` — a clamped card never renders at AX5 *by design*, so the row asked for an observation the design forbids, and no amount of environment-forcing would have produced it. Row 5b now captures at the card's **ceiling**, plus one capture requested at AX5 asserted **equal** to it (that equality is the clamp binding, and is the only AX5 claim this design permits). Also restated F2's wrap check as geometry — the pill stays one line and stays **contained within** the card's frame — because mid-token wrap is invisible to `.label`, which is the whole reason F2 shipped. The existing `HeatModalCardLayoutGuardTests` greps stay, explicitly demoted to regression backstop, explicitly unable to discharge the row.
- **Finding 4 ruling — not an accepted limitation; the clock gets injected, and it is a 2-line seam, not an abstraction.** `HourFormat.readout(now:)` and `DensityStore(now:)` **already take an injected clock**; only the composition root hardcodes `Date()` (`MapScreen.swift:177` and the defaulted `DensityStore()` at `:89`). So the cost of determinism here is one launch-argument-fed `Date` passed to two existing parameters. Against that: the "next day" pill is row 5b's *stated positive control* and the exact element F1 truncated, and it renders only after local noon — meaning the row **reported a pass while its own control was absent for half of every day**, the same shape as an empty-set pass condition. Time-gating or skipping the test would have written that gap into the gate permanently.
- **Whole-table re-audit (L-047), which is where most of the actual defects were.** v4's own scope note admitted rows 1–7 were never checked against the three standing rules; an amendment re-audits everything, so I did. Found and fixed, same commit: **row 6(c)** carried the *identical* stale-AX5 defect as 5b **and** listed "no clipping or truncation" as a pass condition at layer *unit* — unobservable through `.exists`/`.label`, deleted and pointed at row 5b's captures; **row 2(a)** ("identical for the same hour") passes over two empty arrays — now requires ≥3 non-`.clear` fills recorded; **row 2(d)**, **row 3** (a grep over an empty diff returns zero for the forbidden token too) and **rows 7(b)/(c)/(d1)/(d2)** (four *unchanged*/*nothing appeared* claims that all pass identically if the gesture never reached the app) each gained a positive control; **row 5**'s "the now mark differs in **shape**" restated as a recorded ≥2pt frame-dimension difference at a stated layer. Rows 1 and 4 hold as written.
- **New build step C15** — `UITestOverrides`, two launch-argument reads at one composition root, both defaulting to today's behaviour. Recorded in §10 as a **deliberate accepted risk** (test-only branches in shipping code) with its own **[ASSUMPTION]** stated: that root-level `.environment(\.dynamicTypeSize,…)` propagates into `HeatModalCard` and is then clamped by its own modifier is standard SwiftUI behaviour but **not observed live by this pass** — if `ios-developer` finds otherwise, the honest outcome is a **BLOCKED** disclosure written into row 5b, never a fallback to the grep.
- **Simulator fact filed where the next role will find it (L-046).** The content-size limitation lived only inside comments in `SearchAccessibilityTests.swift` and `HeatModalCardLayoutGuardTests.swift` — which is exactly why it was re-derived twice — so it is now a bullet in `passenger-code/CLAUDE.md`'s **Simulator facts**, stated together with the route that *does* work, so the next reader doesn't take "content size can't be forced" as "Dynamic Type can't be tested."

### 2026-08-07 — product — T-048/`PAS-35` Local threshold acceptance: ACCEPT (value 2 stands, and is forced rather than chosen)

- **Verdict: ACCEPT.** The DoD ("value confirmed or changed at the single declaration site") is met. Task moves to `aviran-review`, not straight to `done`. `chief-of-staff` owns writing this to `PAS-35` and `BOARD.md`; I touched neither.
- **Re-derived from source, not from `qa`'s report.** `grep -rn threshold --include=*.swift Passenger` → one declaration, `Passenger/Passport/LocalStatus.swift:27` (`static let threshold = 2`); the four other hits (`PassportLabels`, `PassportProgressList` ×2, `LocalStatus.isLocal`) all *read* `LocalStatus.threshold` — no second literal compared against a Been count anywhere, which is req 4's last bullet and TRD §9 row 4(d). The doc comment's stale **[ASSUMPTION]** / "Aviran's to set" text is gone and now states decision #45's reasoning — that was D6's one named code follow-up, and it is done.
- **Fixture re-derived independently** (`python3` over the three shipped JSONs, field names read from the files rather than assumed — `hood_id`/`place_id`/`kind`, not the camelCase the report implies): 44 Hoods, exactly `florentin`/`kerem-hateimanim`/`neve-tzedek` designated; 9 places, 3/3/3 in exactly those Hoods; 2 `been` visits, both attributed to `kerem-hateimanim`. So `kerem-hateimanim` → Local, the other two → 0, overall → false. Genuine variance, as `qa` found.
- **The product call, which the DoD asked for and is the substance of this pass: 2 is forced, not chosen.** Decision #45 bounded the value to [2, 3] — floor 2 (at 1 Local is true on first contact), ceiling "the smallest curated place count across designated Hoods, 3 today" — then rejected 3 for equalling 100% catalogue completion with zero margin. **That ceiling counted rows, not places a person can go to.** `kerem-carmel-spice-corner` and `neve-nachum-gutman-museum` are `permanently_closed: true`, so `kerem-hateimanim` and `neve-tzedek` hold **2 open places each, not 3**. The real range is **[2, 2]**. Two consequences, both recorded rather than left implied: 2 is the only admissible value, so the verdict cannot be anything but ACCEPT; and the zero-margin property that disqualified 3 is *already true of 2* in two of three Hoods — which no threshold value can fix, because none smaller is admissible. **The correction lands on the dataset, not the number:** those two Hoods need a third open curated place to restore margin.
- **Spec defects fixed in this same commit (L-009).** The reachability criterion existed in `hood-dataset` req 5 (added at T-047 acceptance) but `passport.md` still contradicted it in two places, so a reader of the owning PRD would still ship the blind version: (1) req 4 gained a pass/fail bullet stating the **rendered consequence** — every designated Hood's row must be reachable to Local by visiting places open today; a row pinned below Local wherever the user goes is a dataset defect, not a UI state; (2) the data-sourcing line's "≥2 curated places" corrected to ≥2 **open** places, naming why the row count is not a guard (it stays green even if every place in a Hood closes). PRD → **Draft v4**. Decision #45 amended in `strategy/decisions.md` with a marked, appended amendment — value unchanged, ceiling corrected, review trigger widened to fire on a **closure**, not only on catalogue growth. `passenger-strategy.md` untouched (Aviran-gated, rule 8).

Cited rather than duplicated. This pass closes the *spec* half of the same blind spot, which T-068 does not cover.

Passport is V1-authorized verbatim — *"a stamp per Been place, contributing toward 'Local' status **per Hood** in a set of hoods Passenger designates"* (`strategy/passenger-strategy.md`, V1 scope, Passport bullet) — and that same clause puts the parameterisation with the company, which is why #45 was not escalated. ### 2026-08-07 — ios-code-reviewer — PAS-51 (T-032 orphaned F1/F2 fix): **APPROVE WITH MINORS**

- **Did:** first-ever code review of `passenger-code 927784b` (`HourReadout.swift` gains `.accessibilityIdentifier("hourReadout")`; new `PassengerTests/HeatModalCardLayoutGuardTests.swift` + `PassengerUITests/HeatModalCardLayoutTests.swift`), reviewed against `prds/time-slider/TRD.md` §2.3 (chrome layering) and §9 row 5b (the rendered-frame verification row added at T-055 specifically because F1/F2 slipped past every prior gate). Read `BOARD.md`'s T-032 row + PAS-51 lines and the full F1/F2 history in this file first (2026-08-03 REJECT, 2026-08-04 founder-direct override, 2026-08-04 `c1b8bc3` fixup where the actual `HeatModalCard.swift` constants landed unreviewed as disclosed PAS-15 rode-along content, 2026-08-06 `ios-developer` landing this commit). Also read `HeatModalCard.swift` in full — it is **not** part of this diff (constants `navRowBandHeight`/`gapAboveNavRow`/`maxDynamicTypeSize` already on `main` since `c1b8bc3`) but is what F1/F2's actual fix consists of, so I reviewed it as the effective implementation under test even though this commit doesn't touch it.
- **Independent build+test, not trusted from the commit message:** isolated `git worktree` pinned to `927784b`, dedicated simulator (`pas51-verify`, iOS 26.5, deleted after), dedicated `-derivedDataPath` (deleted after), per L-029. First run of `-only-testing:PassengerUITests/HeatModalCardLayoutTests` **failed** — `hourSlider never rendered` after tapping Heat, at `uptime` load average 407 (four other sessions' concurrent `xcodebuild` processes confirmed via `ps aux`, consistent with this repo's documented shared-machine contention). Diagnosed rather than accepted: reran the identical scoped test alone once load eased — **passed clean, 31.4s**, hourReadout/Heat/Search/Profile frames all resolved and the non-intersection assertion held. Read as environmental flake, not a defect, per this codebase's own established pattern (L-029) — a second, unmodified rerun flipping pass/fail on the same binary is the signature of contention, not of a race in the code under test. The two `HeatModalCardLayoutGuardTests` (Swift Testing) passed cleanly on the first attempt, no retry needed. Independently confirmed the source-level claims: `gapAboveNavRow: CGFloat = 16`, `.padding(.bottom, Self.navRowBandHeight + Self.gapAboveNavRow)`, `maxDynamicTypeSize: DynamicTypeSize = .accessibility3`, `.dynamicTypeSize(...Self.maxDynamicTypeSize)` all present exactly as the guard test's string-match asserts. `MapNavRow`'s three buttons' accessibility labels (`"Heat"`/`"Search"`/`"Profile"`) match what the UI test queries.
- **F1 — genuinely fixed, genuinely verified.** The actual rendered defect (nav row drawing over the readout at default text size) does not reproduce: I watched the real assertion pass against a real rendered frame, independently reproduced, not inherited from the commit's own claimed 518/518.
- **F2 — fixed by a sound mechanism, but under-verified against what §9 row 5b actually demands, and one comment overstates its own evidence.** Findings, none blocking on their own, taken together they're the "minors":
  1. **No live UI-test coverage for AX5 exists anywhere for this surface** — by the commit's own admission (`HeatModalCardLayoutGuardTests.swift`'s doc comment), because `-UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName` and pre-launch `simctl ui content_size` don't reliably take on this Xcode/iOS build. The substitute is a source-string grep asserting the `.accessibility3` ceiling constant is wired in — which is exactly what row 5b's own verification-method column rules out ("**Not** unit, **not** source review, **not** `exists`"). The substitution is plausible (same construction as `SearchRowGrowthGuardTests`/`PassportAbsenceGateTests` for the identical documented Simulator limitation) but it is a **silent deviation from an explicit TRD row**, never written back into `TRD.md` §9 the way row 5b itself got a T-055 amendment when the original F1/F2 gap was found. Per this repo's own L-009 pattern (three prior instances of "the rule existed, the row didn't"), this should get the same treatment: either amend §9 row 5b to formally accept the structural-guard substitution for the AX5 half (citing the Simulator limitation), or route to `architect`/`product` to decide otherwise.
  2. **`HeatModalCard.swift`'s own comment claims verification evidence that doesn't appear to exist in this repo's audit trail.** `maxDynamicTypeSize`'s doc comment states the AX3 cap was "confirmed by rendering the full … readout at AX3, AX4, and AX5 on device (screenshots in the T-032 rebuild's PR/worklog)." I searched `PROGRESS.md` for any `ios-developer` entry documenting that build pass — none exists; the constants landed inside `c1b8bc3`, explicitly flagged to the reviewer of that commit as PAS-15 content **not to review**, and no dedicated F1/F2 rebuild worklog entry was ever written. The claimed screenshots may be real and simply uncited, but as written this is an unverifiable evidence claim in shipped source, the same shape of problem L-030 exists to catch on the review side.
  3. **The F1 UI test has no positive control**, contra row 5b's explicit standing rule 2 requirement (the pill reads `"next day"` in full, the numeral reads `"+12h"` in full). `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` means the three sub-elements aren't individually queryable, which reasonably subsumes row 5b's *per-element intersection* requirement (a non-intersecting bounding box implies no sub-element intersects either) — but it does not substitute for asserting `readout.label`/content, which the shipped test never does.
  4. **The "next day" scenario is wall-clock-dependent, not deterministic.** `MapScreen.swift` calls `now: Date()` directly with no injectable clock reachable from a UI-test launch argument; the test's `slider.adjust(toNormalizedSliderPosition: 1.0)` only lands on an `isNextDay == true` reading when the test happens to run at local hour ≥ 12. It passed this session because it happened to run at 13:33 local; run before noon, it would still assert non-intersection but would never render the "next day" pill — the exact element F1's regression truncated. The docstring's claim to "reproduce product's exact rejection scenario" is only sometimes true.
  5. No runtime assertion of `HeatModalCard.frame.maxY < safe-area bottom` (row 5b's requirement iii, "`bottom: 0` falsified by name") — covered only by the same source-review-style guard test as point 1.
- **Verdict: APPROVE WITH MINORS.** F1, the more severe of the two rejected defects (wrong-hour misreading via truncation), is solidly fixed and independently reproduced passing on a real rendered app. F2 rests on a standard, reliable SwiftUI mechanism (`DynamicTypeSize` range clamping) that is very likely correct even without a fresh live re-check, and the Simulator limitation blocking that re-check is real and precedented elsewhere in this codebase — but the verification trail around it needs to be honest and TRD-conformant rather than implicit. Not blocking because nothing here is an observed regression; routing to `qa` with the five points above as the explicit brief, plus a TRD/comment cleanup nudge back to whoever owns row 5b.
- **Evidence:** `passenger-code 927784b` reviewed in full (`git show`). Isolated worktree build+test: `HeatModalCardLayoutGuardTests` 2/2 passed (first attempt); `HeatModalCardLayoutTests` 1/1 passed (second attempt, first attempt's failure attributed to load average 407 from concurrent sessions, confirmed via `ps aux`/`uptime`). `HeatModalCard.swift` source read in full for the effective F1/F2 implementation. `PROGRESS.md` searched for corroborating F2 on-device evidence — none found.
- **Left behind:** for `qa` — re-run `HeatModalCardLayoutTests` once more on a quieter machine to get a clean first-pass green (not required for this verdict, just cleaner evidence); consider adding the missing positive-control assertion and/or a deterministic next-day fixture if picked up as a follow-up rather than blocking on it now. For `architect`/`product` — decide whether §9 row 5b's AX5 half gets a formal TRD amendment accepting the structural-guard substitution, matching the T-055 precedent. For whoever touches `HeatModalCard.swift` next — either find and cite the claimed on-device AX3/AX4/AX5 screenshots, or soften the comment to not claim evidence this repo's history can't produce.

### 2026-08-07 — developer — Hood alias mechanism (unowned finding, `data-engineer` 2026-08-07): schema built, migration `009`

- **Did:** picked up the unowned finding on `BOARD.md` (`data-engineer`'s Tel Aviv coverage-gap follow-up, `hood-dataset` PRD Decisions log 2026-08-07 "Groups 4/5" entry): 6 real Tel Aviv neighbourhood names have no separate Hood geometry (2 are OSM-identical duplicates, 4 resolve fully inside an already-shipped Hood's polygon) and were unfindable by search because `hoods` had no alias/alt-name mechanism at all. This was flagged explicitly as a schema decision for `developer`, not `data-engineer`, to make.
- **Decision:** `hoods.aliases text[] not null default '{}'` — a column, not a separate `hood_aliases` table. Every confirmed case is a plain same-script alternate name with no per-alias provenance/locale need; a join table is the correct escalation the day that changes, and this column doesn't foreclose adding one later. Full reasoning in `prds/hood-dataset/TRD.md` §8 D11 (new).
- **Built:**
  - `database/migrations/009_hoods_aliases.sql` — additive, `if not exists`-guarded, no RLS change (inherits `001` A2's public-read policy, column-agnostic). Independent of `003`/`006`-`008` — applies in any order relative to them, only needs `001` (the `hoods` table itself).
  - `database/scripts/validate_dataset.py` — `HoodRecord` gains `aliases`; `load_hood_source` parses the optional per-hood `aliases` field (defaults `[]`); new **V10** check: each alias non-empty, no duplicate within a Hood (case-insensitive), no alias collides case-insensitively with any Hood's own `id`/`name` or another Hood's alias anywhere in the dataset. Verified V10 fires correctly against two synthetic bad-data cases (duplicate-within-hood, cross-hood collision) before trusting it on the real 44-row source.
  - `database/scripts/build_hoods.py` — emits `aliases` (text array, `'{}'::text[]` when empty) in both generated artifacts: the migration SQL insert/upsert (`aliases = excluded.aliases` added to the `on conflict` clause) and the iOS bundle JSON. Bundle `schemaVersion` bumped 2 → 3 (decode-compatible in both directions per the TRD's own rule — an unknown higher version is never rejected).
  - `prds/hood-dataset/TRD.md` amended: new top-line `**Amended:** 2026-08-07`, §3.1 (schema), §3.2 (source-file `aliases` field + rule), §3.3 (generated SQL example), §3.5 (bundle v3), §5.2 (V10 row), new **§8 D11** (the decision writeup, including the explicit "`Ohel Moshe` is not a confirmed alias" caveat pulled from `data-engineer`'s later re-investigation). `TRD.html` regenerated via `prds/md2html.py` to match.

- **F1 — blocking, req 3 bullet 5 ("Sticker shape matches the place's type — a coffee cup for a café", decision #29).** The shipped stickers are abstract geometry: `StickerShape` is `circle, square, triangle, diamond, star, hexagon, generic` with `symbolName` returning `circle.fill`/`triangle.fill`/…, and `Resources/place-types-tel-aviv.json` maps `cafe→circle`, `restaurant→triangle`, `bar→diamond`, `market→square`, `museum→hexagon`, `landmark→star`. A café's sticker is a plain filled circle. That is a bijection, not a match — nothing about a circle says café — and the requirement's own worked example is the pass condition it fails. Verified by reading `Passenger/Places/StickerShape.swift` and the registry at `1903eb1` directly, plus the nine shipped places and their `place_type` values.
- **F2 — blocking, req 7 bullet 1 ("a VoiceOver label naming the place and its type"), and this is the D12 ruling I was asked for.** `PassportLabels.sticker` composes `"\(placeName), \(shape.spokenName) sticker"` over `spokenName` = `"circle"/"square"/"triangle"/…`, so a screen-reader user hears *"Dr. Shakshuka, triangle sticker"*. A geometry word is not a type. **D12's premise is rejected, not confirmed:** it argued req 7 and `places-dataset` §4.4 (*"no user-facing surface renders `place_type`"*) "cannot both be satisfied literally." They can. §4.4 forbids rendering the raw server vocabulary string; it does not forbid naming what a place is in the app's own words. The contradiction existed only because the shape vocabulary was chosen abstract first — a depictive glyph's spoken noun ("cutlery", "cup") names the type in substance while rendering no `place_type` string, satisfying both documents. So D12 is rejected along with its cause rather than ruled on in isolation. It is downstream of F1 but stated separately because fixing F1 alone would still leave the geometry word spoken.
- **Where it was lost, and the L-009 fix made in this same commit:** TRD §9 row 3's pass condition for that bullet is *"every registry key maps to a non-`.generic` case whose `symbolName` resolves"* — totality and symbol resolution, never depiction. So the requirement was weakened at the TRD layer and no gate downstream had anything objective to fail it on; `qa` correctly reports PASS against the checks it was handed. Per L-009 the missing criteria were written in the same commit as the verdict, stated as the rendered consequence and labelled as added at acceptance: `passport` req 3 gained a name-hidden depiction test that explicitly fails a distinct-but-abstract shape per type, and req 7 gained the *"cutlery sticker" passes / "triangle sticker" fails* bullet. `places-dataset` req 3 gained the matching bullet in the same pass (Job 0 item 4 — its own two bullets guarantee coverage and say nothing about what the shape shows, which is the upstream half of the same blind spot, and B1's ratified vocabulary is where the pairing is fixed). `passport` → Draft v3; decisions-log rows on both PRDs.
- **Not a scope or taste call, and no founder ratification is being overruled:** the registry's own `_note` says PROVISIONAL pending Aviran's T-042 B1, so no ratified vocabulary exists yet. But B1 ratifies the JSON's *values*; the six abstract cases live in client Swift (`StickerShape`), so no ratification can turn "circle" into a cup — the fix is a code change in T-037's own C2, not a wait on T-042. Specific glyph choices stay provisional under B1 exactly as today.
- **The other six P0s hold, re-derived independently at `1903eb1` (`git archive`, not the shared dirty tree — several sessions have WIP in it, incl. `MapScreen.swift`):** req 1 — zero hits across all nine social/account/network symbols, zero non-`systemName` `Image(`, zero `UserDefaults`/`FileManager`; req 2 — `onProfileTap: openPassport` wired at `MapScreen.swift:526`, zero `camera`/`selectedHour` reads in `Passport/`; req 4 — `progress` filters `designatedForProgression` so undesignated Hoods are absent not zero, `isOverallLocal` guards the empty set explicitly rather than relying on `allSatisfy`, zero retired tier names, exactly one `threshold` declaration (`LocalStatus.threshold = 2`); req 5 — `PassportProgressList` renders `Text("\(beenCount) of \(threshold)")` always plus a `Label("Local")` word-and-glyph, empty state is icon + one line, no bar/lock/teaser; req 6 — zero interruption presenters, no observer on `visits`; req 8 — zero `CoreLocation`/authorization/network symbols. Req 3's other bullets (Been-only, one-per-place, revisit-adds-none, no shapeless sticker, one city page) all hold — only the depiction bullet fails.

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Requirement-by-requirement:
1. **Cartoon ice cream truck (P0) — PASS on subject, partial on style.** Subject is unambiguous: rounded cargo box + cab, glass serving window, scalloped pink/green/orange awning, glossy hubcap wheels, soft-serve-cone-on-a-cherry roof ornament. Reads as "ice cream truck" instantly. **Style is the one place I'd push back and am deliberately not rejecting on** — see the reservation below.
2. **Light background matching the reference's light rounded-square treatment (P0) — PASS.** Light-blue vertical gradient with a soft top-left highlight.

4. **Builds and shows on the home screen — PASS.** Accepted `ios-developer`'s build+install+screenshot evidence (`e1f0714`) rather than re-running the full cycle, and independently corroborated the part that doesn't need a build: downscaled the asset to true home-screen and Spotlight sizes (180px = 60pt@3x, 120px = 60pt@2x, 87px = 29pt@3x, Lanczos) and inspected each. Truck silhouette, cone, awning band, green stripe and wheels all still read at 87px. Two independent methods agreeing, not one report echoed.

- **On the three flagged open items — two now closed with measurements, one deliberately left open:**
  1. **No reference image was ever seen by any agent — NOT resolved, and not resolvable by me.** I judged against the text description on its own terms, which is all that exists. My ACCEPT is explicitly bounded: it certifies the icon is a well-executed cartoon ice cream truck on a light background that builds, ships and reads at every real size — **it cannot certify fidelity to an image nobody in this chain has seen.** Only Aviran can close that, and `aviran-review` is exactly the gate for it. Per L-013 I'm also not treating the reference's descriptive specifics ("high-gloss 3D render aesthetic") as founder-given: `chief-of-staff`'s own stub states plainly there is no verified transcript of Aviran's literal wording, so that phrasing is a recorder's description of an unseen image, **[ASSUMPTION]**-grade, and I've declined to reason hard from it.
